author: NorthEast News Desk
body: South Africa defeated New Zealand 43-28 in Baltimore on Saturday, winning for a third consecutive weekend to claim the four-test “Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry” series 3-1. The world champion Springboks scored six tries in the finale before an announced crowd of 68,173 at M&T Bank Stadium.

Damian de Allende, Morne van den Berg, Malcolm Marx, Pieter-Steph du Toit, Kurt-Lee Arendse and Cameron Hanekom crossed for South Africa. New Zealand captain Codie Taylor scored the opening try, with Will Jordan, Ethan Blackadder and Beauden Barrett also finding the try line for the All Blacks.

South Africa led 17-14 at halftime and created its decisive advantage after bringing on its replacement forwards early in the second half. Marx and du Toit scored in quick succession to make it 29-14. The Baltimore match ended New Zealand’s eight-game, six-week tour connected to the rivalry series, the first extended tour of its kind in 30 years.
dek: South Africa scored six tries before 68,173 spectators and completed the four-test rivalry series with a 3-1 record.
headline: Springboks beat All Blacks 43-28 in Baltimore to clinch series
